function.name: web_search
function.description: Search for current or unknown facts, or when asked to search. Answer settled knowledge without searching. For a supplied URL use fetch_url. Use snippets if sufficient; open a result for missing details. Reuse earlier evidence when sufficient. For pictures use show_pictures.

query.description: What to look up, as you would type it into a search box

function.name: fetch_url
function.description: Read a public URL from the user, search results, or earlier conversation. Open supplied URLs directly; never invent one. After search, open only for missing details, verification or a requested summary. Reuse text already read. If a page fails, search for another source. Use find to locate details on a long page.

url.description: The full https address of the page to read

save_to.description: Optional file path to save the page's text into the shared folder for scripts

find.description: Optional. A word, phrase or regular expression to look for. Only the parts of the page that match it come back, with a little text around each, instead of the start of the page

function.name: show_pictures
function.description: Show pictures or short clips found on the web, as thumbnails to display rather than text to read. It answers no questions; for information of any kind use web_search.

kind.description: Pictures or clips. Defaults to images.

function.name: run_script
function.description: Run a JavaScript program in a sandbox and use what it returns. For real computation: arithmetic, dates, regex, JSON, or a file too large to read whole. Give source, or path to a saved .js file. Modern JavaScript with await; no network; require('fs') and require('path') only, for files you named in files. The last expression is the answer.

source.description: The JavaScript to run. The last expression is the answer.

path.description: Instead of source, a .js file to run

files.description: Paths in the shared folder to read in as inputs

function.name: find_files
function.description: Find files in the shared folder by a name pattern like *.md, optionally containing given text. Not for reading a file whose path you have. If nothing was named to look for, ask rather than guess.

pattern.description: A file name or a pattern such as *.md or notes*

contains.description: Optional text that must appear inside the file

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read the text of a file in the folder the user shared. Use the path exactly as find_files gave it. If no path is known, ask which file rather than inventing one.

path.description: The file's path inside the shared folder, like notes/todo.md. Text only

offset.description: Characters to skip, to read further into a long file

function.name: write_file
function.description: Save a file into the folder the user shared. Pass replace to overwrite one that exists, which is how to fix and re-save a script. If no path is given, ask where.

path.description: Where to save it, like notes/summary.md

content.description: The whole text of the file

replace.description: True to overwrite an existing file

function.name: delete_file
function.description: Delete a file or folder from the folder the user shared. Use it to clean up files you created that are no longer needed. Deleting a folder deletes everything in it.

function.name: show_website
function.description: Show an HTML page you saved, rendered live. Point it at the page's path, like site/index.html. Its folder is served whole, so relative links to CSS, scripts and images in it work, and nothing loads from the network: keep every script, style, font and image in the folder or inline. Call it once after the first save; later saves update the page by themselves.

path.description: The HTML file to show, like site/index.html

function.name: show_document
function.description: Show a Markdown file you saved as A4 pages, like notes/report.md. Call it once after the first save; later saves with replace update the pages live.

path.description: The Markdown file to show, like notes/report.md

function.name: show_slides
function.description: Show a Markdown file as a 16:9 slide deck, slides separated by a line containing only ---. Call it once after the first save; later saves with replace update the deck live.

path.description: The Markdown deck to show, like talk/slides.md

function.name: save_memory
function.description: Save one short fact about the user for future conversations: a preference, a name, how they like answers written. Only what stays true after this conversation, never what was just said.

fact.description: One sentence, third person, like 'Prefers answers without preamble'

function.name: update_memory
function.description: Rewrite one saved fact about the user that is outdated or wrong.

old.description: The saved fact to rewrite, as read_memory shows it

new.description: One sentence, third person, that replaces it

function.name: forget_memory
function.description: Delete one saved fact about the user, when they ask to forget it or it no longer applies.

fact.description: The saved fact to delete, as read_memory shows it

function.name: read_memory
function.description: Read the short facts saved about this user in earlier conversations. Call it before answering anything that depends on who the user is or what they prefer.

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Ask the user a question when the request could mean more than one thing, or when a detail a tool needs was never given. Suggest up to four options. Not for a request no tool can carry out: say plainly that you cannot.

question.description: The question to put to the user, in one sentence

options.description: Up to four short answers to offer, or none

multiple.description: True when more than one option may be chosen

function.name: advance
function.description: Mark one step of the plan finished, by its number.

step.description: The number of the step that is now done, as the plan lists it
